newsitem.title: UK: Cuba sugar freight business keeps market busy.
newsitem.headline: Cuba sugar freight business keeps market busy.

text.p: Cuba and other Latin American origins again set the tone on the sugar freight market on Tuesday as various new orders emerged to keep the market busy before Europe's Easter holiday break.
For Cuba, the Black Sea plus the standard north Africa options were the principal quoted destinations.
"There's quite a lot of business being done there," said one shipbroker, adding that while charterers were expecting rates of between $27 amd $28, shipowners were looking for rates nearer to $30.
The last reported fixture on the route fetched $31.50, he said.

Physical sugar brokers have said Cuba is lagging behind with its sugar shipments this year, suggesting that island could be overstretching itself on its supply contracts for the 1997/98 cane sugar crop.

Express Sea Transport entered the market on account to ship 25/27,000 tonnes in bulk from Cuba to the Black Sea for 1/10 April, after having reportedly fixed on the same route last week. Further details were not available.
Of the day's other new business, Sugar Exporters quoted for 12/14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from south Brazil to Lagos for mid-April shipment dates.
Commodity Specialists were open for a prompt 5/10,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from La Romana to Puerto Rico.
Genoc quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Poland to the Red Sea with options of Mediterranean and Colombo, again for prompt shipment.
Shipbrokers said Seven Seas was still open with its prompt/onwards bagged order from Djibouti to Somalia.
In other news, Bangladesh bought 25,000 tonnes of white sugar for shipment by May 15, with the first 12,500-tonne instalment expected to reach Chittagong by May 8 and the rest by May 15.
The supplier was named as G. Premjee.
